sections.title: Why Use a LIC Jeevan Labh Premium Calculator?

content.text: This tool empowers you to make informed decisions by providing instant clarity on costs and benefits. Here’s why it’s essential:

items: Fast & Accurate Premiums: Get immediate, reliable premium estimates for your chosen sum assured and term.
Compare Scenarios: Easily check how your premium changes for a ₹10 lakh cover versus a ₹1 crore cover.
Budgeting Made Easy: Instantly see the difference between monthly, quarterly, and yearly payment modes.
Full Cost Transparency: Understand the impact of GST and optional riders on your total premium outflow.

sections.title: Factors That Affect Your Jeevan Labh Premium

items: Age of Policyholder: The younger you are, the lower your premium.
Sum Assured: A higher coverage amount means a higher premium.
Policy Term: Longer terms generally have slightly lower annualized premiums but are paid for more years.
Mode of Payment: Yearly payments are cheaper than monthly payments due to 'modal loading'.
Riders: Optional add-ons like Accidental Death Benefit increase the cost.
High Sum Assured Rebates: LIC offers a discount on higher sum assured amounts, which our calculator includes.

sections.title: LIC Jeevan Labh Benefits at a Glance

items: Pay for Less, Get for More: The key benefit is the limited premium payment term. For a 25-year policy, you only pay for 16 years.
Dual Advantage: It combines life insurance protection with a disciplined savings plan, ensuring a lump sum at maturity.
Tax Efficiency: Premiums paid are deductible under Section 80C, and the maturity amount is tax-free under Section 10(10D).
Liquidity Options: Loan and surrender facilities are available after two full years of premium payments.

items.q: What is the premium of LIC Jeevan Labh for 10 lakh?
items.a: For a 30-year-old taking a 25-year term, the yearly premium for a ₹10 lakh cover is approximately ₹42,200. This can be calculated instantly using our Jeevan Labh 936 calculator online free.

items.q: How is LIC Jeevan Labh maturity value calculated?
items.a: The maturity value is the sum of the Basic Sum Assured, all vested Simple Reversionary Bonuses declared over the policy term, and a one-time Final Additional Bonus (FAB), if any. Our LIC Jeevan Labh maturity calculator estimates this for you.

items.q: What are LIC Jeevan Labh bonus rates 2025?
items.a: Bonus rates are declared by LIC annually and are not guaranteed. For recent years, the illustrative rate for Jeevan Labh has been in the range of ₹43-₹47 per ₹1,000 Sum Assured, depending on the policy term.

items.q: Which is better: LIC Jeevan Labh or Jeevan Umang?
items.a: Jeevan Labh is a limited-pay endowment plan with a fixed maturity date, ideal for goal-based savings. Jeevan Umang is a whole-life plan that provides annual survival benefits after the PPT and matures at age 100. Umang has higher premiums but offers lifelong cover and income. Use a Jeevan Labh vs Jeevan Umang calculator for a detailed comparison.

items.q: Can I take a loan on my LIC Jeevan Labh policy?
items.a: Yes, a loan can be availed on the policy after at least two full years' premiums have been paid, subject to terms and conditions.

items.q: Is LIC Jeevan Labh a good investment?
items.a: Jeevan Labh is a safe, traditional insurance-cum-savings product offering tax-free returns of around 5-6% IRR. It's suitable for risk-averse individuals seeking disciplined savings and life cover, but not for those seeking high, market-linked growth. A good return calculator can illustrate this.

items.q: How much is LIC Jeevan Labh 1 crore premium?
items.a: For a 30-year-old with a 25-year term, the yearly premium for a ₹1 crore sum assured is approximately ₹4,15,000. Use our calculator to get an exact figure for your age.

items.q: What is the surrender value in Jeevan Labh?
items.a: The policy acquires a surrender value after two full years of premium payment. A Jeevan Labh surrender value calculator would show the Guaranteed Surrender Value (a percentage of total premiums paid) and the Special Surrender Value, which depends on LIC's discretion and is usually higher.
